source: hand-authored fixture for issue #309 — not shipped data
description: Shapes about whether a CONDITION rule's bare-containment match against a recorded condition is corroborated, for the injected record's patient-specific reading. The recorded condition names are real: every one is a concept name from the OpenMRS 3.7.1 reference-application demo dictionary, which is the corpus issue #309's measurement was run over. (1) Naltrexone rules on the condition token 'liver', which is the most plausible hepatic contraindication token there is and which nests inside every deliver/delivery form the dictionary publishes — 20 of the 30 values it matches over that dictionary's 2581 condition candidates, e.g. 'Status Post Cesarean Delivery'. (2) Metformin rules on 'renal', which nests inside 'Malignant tumor of adrenal gland' — a tumour of a different organ. (3) Ibuprofen rules on 'peptic ulcer', which is one of the four condition tokens the SHIPPED curated seed publishes; over both measured corpora every one of its matches carries it as a whole word, which is the loss side of the boundary rule and is zero. (4) Paracetamol rules on 'edema', whose mid-word matches are clinically RIGHT compounds ('Lymphedema', 'Angioedema') — the residue the boundary rule gives up, kept here so a future change can read what it costs. No entry carries ATC codes or interactions, so no class comparison can chip and every record is the contraindication arms' own.
